A four-round grilling locked these decisions: - **Approach:** Rebuild in dai's *design idiom* with our *own information architecture* — NOT a fork, NOT a transcription. No file copied from the reference; his name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere. - **LEDGER contract retired:** Both `DESIGN.md` and `CONTEXT.md` rewritten from scratch. - **No registry:** No component registry, blocks, sponsors, awards, certifications, testimonials, or bookmarks — the IA is sized to real proof. - **Scratch scope:** Delete `app/`, `components/`, LEDGER-specific `lib/` files, and `globals.css`; rebuild the design system from zero. Port back three survivors: the `/writings → /blog` 301, the feed/sitemap/robots routes, and the `rehype-sanitize` MDX hardening. - **Home:** Single dense scroll — Masthead → AI Activity → Projects → footer. Sub-routes for Blog only. - **Blog:** Fully wired (MDX, RSS) but hidden until a real Post exists. - **Heatmap:** Kept and redesigned as the density anchor / signature element. - **Tagline:** `agentic engineer`. - **Avatar:** No portrait exists; spec'd as a *designed absence* — reserved footprint with live cursor-light interaction, so a portrait drops in later with zero layout shift. - **Projects:** 8 curated (relunar, pi-queue, offdex, gunmetal, mdv-ts, block, codexchat, openutm-v0). - **No "Now / currently building" block.** Final instruction: "Go ahead and do the full complete rewrite… Make it completely without stopping and make sure everything works perfectly and everything looks utterly beautiful and with perfect front end utterly best design." **No new user messages arrived in this continuation segment** — it was pure execution of that instruction. 2. **Key Technical Concepts:** - Next.js 16.2.10 App Router (Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript 5.8, Tailwind CSS v4 (`@import "tailwindcss"`, `@custom-variant`, `@theme inline`), bun 1.3.13 as package manager and test runner - `next-themes` (`attribute="class"`, `enableSystem={false}`, `storageKey="theme"`), `document.startViewTransition` for theme crossfade - `useSyncExternalStore(noSubscribe, () => true, () => false)` as the lint-clean "is hydrated" hook (replaces `useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])`, which trips `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` in eslint-config-next 16) - `react-hooks/refs` rule: reading a ref inside a `useCallback` that is referenced from JSX during render is an error; fix is to move ref reads into effect cleanups - `next-mdx-remote/rsc` + `rehype-sanitize` + `sugar-high`; `@vercel/blob` for AI activity payload with `next: { revalidate: 3600 }` - oklch color tokens, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, six-step type scale, hairline borders instead of shadows - CSS-only entrance animations (`rule-draw`, `settle`, `cell-in`), `prefers-reduced-motion` keeping colour feedback but removing movement - Geist Sans + Geist Mono (Newsreader dropped) - Heatmap layout: one grid column per week (`grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--weeks), …)`), Sunday-aligned 7-slot columns with null padding, pure-CSS mobile truncation via `.activity-col:nth-child(-n + 26) { display: none }` - Listbox pattern (`role="listbox"` + `role="option"` + `aria-activedescendant` + roving arrow keys) as a single tab stop for 365 cells - Next 16 route params are `Promise<{ slug: string }>` and must be awaited 3. **Files and Code Sections:** **`components/command-palette.tsx`** (created) — Hand-rolled ⌘K palette (cmdk not installed). Exports `CommandItem` type `{ id, group, label, hint?, href?, external?, action?: "toggle-theme" }` and a `matches()` subsequence matcher. Key structure: global `keydown` listener for Meta/Ctrl+K; body scroll lock + input focus in an effect whose **cleanup restores focus** (`restoreTo.current?.focus()`) — this placement is required to satisfy `react-hooks/refs`; `setActive(0)` happens in the input's `onChange`, not an effect. `run()` handles mailto via `window.location.href`, external via `window.open(href, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")`, internal via `router.push`. Renders `PaletteTrigger` (a `hidden sm:flex` ⌘K pill) when closed and both trigger + dialog when open. **`components/site-header.tsx`** (created) — Server component. Sticky blurred bar: ```tsx
{site.handle.toLowerCase()}.com
…navItems(hasPosts)…
``` **`lib/palette.ts`** (created) — `paletteItems(hasPosts: boolean): CommandItem[]` builds groups `go` (Home + nav), `projects` (8, `external: true`, hint = `destinationHost`), `elsewhere` (socials all `external: true`, plus RSS `external: true`), `settings` (theme toggle). Imports `CommandItem` as `import type` so the "use client" module is never pulled in at runtime by bun tests. **`components/site-footer.tsx`** (created) — `mt-24 border-t`, copyright + socials as words + `Rss` icon link. **`components/masthead.tsx`** (created, client) — Pointer-tracking cursor light. `moveLight(clientX, clientY)` computes the slot's `getBoundingClientRect()` and sets `--lx`, `--ly`, `--lit` on the slot; `onPointerMove` is on the whole `
` so the light in the empty avatar follows the cursor anywhere in the masthead. Renders `next/image` with `fill` only when `site.avatar` is non-null. Children carry `style={{ "--i": n } as React.CSSProperties}` to stagger the `.reveal > *` animation. **`lib/activity-grid.ts`** (created) — Pure, testable layout math: ```ts export type ActivityWeek = { key: string; monthLabel?: string; cells: (ActivityDay | null)[] }; export function weekdayIndex(date: string): number // UTC-noon probe, Sunday = 0 export function monthAbbreviation(date: string): string export function formatActivityDate(date: string): string // "Sat, Aug 15, 2026", timeZone: "UTC" export function buildActivityWeeks(days: readonly ActivityDay[]): ActivityWeek[] ``` `buildActivityWeeks` pads the first week with nulls up to `weekdayIndex(days[0].date)`, chunks into 7s, pads the tail, then labels the first week of each new month (never the last column, never a leading stub week). **`components/activity-grid.tsx`** (created, client) — `MOBILE_WEEKS = 27`. Flattens weeks to `slots`, tracks `active: number | null`, `lastFilled`. Container is `role="listbox" tabIndex={0}` with `aria-activedescendant`, `--weeks`/`--weeks-sm` CSS vars, `onFocus` seeding active to `lastFilled`, `onBlur`/`onMouseLeave` clearing, and `onKeyDown` mapping ArrowLeft/Right to ∓7 and ArrowUp/Down to ∓1. Cells are `role="option"` with `aria-label` from `cellLabel(day)`, `data-active`, `data-live`, and `style={{ "--level": \`var(--l${day.intensity})\`, "--col": weekIndex }}`. The readout `

` is `aria-hidden` to avoid double-speak. **`components/activity-section.tsx`** (created, server, async) — Fetches via `getAiActivityPayload()`, materializes with `materializeAiActivity(payload)`, builds weeks, computes `updated` label and `const projecting = activity.days.at(-1)?.live === true;`. Renders the **real lifetime total server-side** (`6,957,491,873` verified in HTML), a five-swatch legend, and a freshness note. **This file has an in-flight edit — see Current Work.** **`components/section-heading.tsx`** (created) — label + optional aside pill + `

`. **`components/projects-section.tsx`** (created) — `id="work"`, `SectionHeading label="work" aside={`${projects.length} selected`}`, `
    ` of `.row-item` anchors with name/language/note, description, and the year→host swap (`.row-year` fades out, `.row-dest` fades in on hover/focus). Footer link "everything else on GitHub". **`app/globals.css`** (edited) — Replaced the activity block. New rules: `.activity-grid` uses `grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--weeks, 53), minmax(0,1fr))`; `.activity-col` is a 7-row grid with `padding-top: 1.05rem`; `.activity-month` is absolutely positioned, allowed to overflow its column; `.activity-cell` keeps the `data-active` outline and `data-live` ring ("Today is a ring, never a fill — a projection must not read as a record"); and: ```css @media (max-width: 40rem) { .activity-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--weeks-sm, 27), minmax(0, 1fr)); } .activity-col:nth-child(-n + 26) { display: none; } } ``` The broken `.activity-cell button, .activity-cell::before { inset: -50% }` hit-area rule was deleted (overlapping pseudo-elements would have blocked neighbour hover). **`app/layout.tsx`** (rewritten) — Dropped Newsreader, `ledger-rules`, `ActivityPulse`/`ActivityTrace`. Computes `const hasPosts = getPublishedPosts().length > 0;` and passes it to `SiteHeader`. `
    ` now carries the container: `className="mx-auto w-full max-w-2xl flex-1 px-5 outline-none sm:px-6"`. Keeps the `.preload` removal script, escaped JSON-LD via `serializeJsonLd`, `profileUrls()` for `sameAs`, `jobTitle: site.tagline`. themeColor updated to `#141416` / `#fbfbfa`. **`app/page.tsx`** (created) — `export const revalidate = 3600;` then ` `. **`app/blog/page.tsx`** (created) — `notFound()` when `getPublishedPosts()` is empty ("Nothing empty is ever shown to a Visitor"). **`app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`** (created) — `type PageProps = { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }`, `generateStaticParams`, `generateMetadata`, BlogPosting JSON-LD via `serializeJsonLd`, back-link, `.rule`, `
    `. **`app/not-found.tsx`** (created) — 404 with back-home link. **`lib/ai-activity.ts`** (edited — the critical fix): ```ts /** Window kept for display: one year of consecutive days ending today. */ export const ACTIVITY_WINDOW_DAYS = 365; export function withLiveToday(history: AiActivity, now = new Date()): AiActivity { const timeZone = history.timezone; const today = calendarDateInTimeZone(now, timeZone); const lastPublished = history.days.at(-1)?.date ?? ""; if (!lastPublished || today <= lastPublished) return history; const fresh = shiftYmd(today, -1) <= lastPublished; const max = Math.max(0, ...history.days.map((d) => d.tokens)); const appended: ActivityDay[] = []; for (let cursor = shiftYmd(lastPublished, 1); cursor <= today; cursor = shiftYmd(cursor, 1)) { if (cursor === today && fresh) { const projection = projectTodayTokens(history.days, now, timeZone); appended.push({ date: today, tokens: projection.tokens, intensity: intensityFromTokens(projection.tokens, max), live: true }); } else { appended.push({ date: cursor, tokens: 0, intensity: 0 }); } } return { days: [...history.days, ...appended].slice(-ACTIVITY_WINDOW_DAYS), lifetimeTokens: history.lifetimeTokens, generatedAt: history.generatedAt, timezone: history.timezone, }; } ``` **`lib/discovery.ts`** (edited) — sitemap core routes now `const routes = posts.length > 0 ? ["", "/blog"] : [""];` with the comment "`/blog` 404s until a Post is published, and `/projects` is a redirect to the Home section — neither belongs in a sitemap while that holds." **`next.config.mjs`** (edited) — added `{ source: "/projects", destination: "/#work", permanent: true }`. **`content/blog/shipping-with-agents.mdx`** (edited) — added `draft: true` to frontmatter. **`components/theme-toggle.tsx`** (edited) — replaced the mounted effect: ```tsx /** Never fires — the snapshot difference alone reports "hydrated". */ const noSubscribe = () => () => {}; const mounted = useSyncExternalStore(noSubscribe, () => true, () => false); ``` **Tests created:** `lib/projects.test.ts` (≤8 projects, https URLs, `destinationHost` = "relunar.com"/"npmjs.com", notes contain no digits), `lib/nav.test.ts`, `lib/palette.test.ts`, `lib/activity-grid.test.ts` (7-slot columns, padding only at ends, 365 filled cells, unique month labels, none on last column), `lib/site.test.ts` (`site.avatar` is null on purpose). **Tests rewritten/updated:** `lib/a11y.test.ts` (now uses `navItems(true)` / `getProjects()`), `lib/discovery.test.ts`, `lib/discovery-smoke.test.ts`, `lib/ai-activity.test.ts` (two new tests: stale-payload zero-fill with no live cell, and the ≤365-day window). 4. **Errors and fixes:** - **`bun test`: `SyntaxError: Export named 'PRIMARY_NAV' not found in module '/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/lib/nav.ts'`** — `lib/a11y.test.ts` referenced the deleted `PRIMARY_NAV`, `getSelectedProjects`, and `getLatestPublishedPosts`. Fixed by rewriting the test against `navItems(true)` and `getProjects()`. - **`discovery-smoke.test.ts` failed** expecting `https://dhruv2mars.com/blog` in the sitemap after the contract change. Fixed by asserting `urls.includes(".../blog") === (getPublishedPosts().length > 0)` and `expect(urls).not.toContain(".../projects")`. - **`bun run typecheck`: `.next/dev/types/validator.ts(80,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../../app/projects/page.js'`** — stale Next-generated route types from the deleted `/projects` route. Fixed with `rm -rf .next`. - **`bun run lint`: 3 errors.** (a) `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on `useEffect(() => setActive(0), [query])` → moved into the input's `onChange`. (b) `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on `useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])` → replaced with `useSyncExternalStore`. (c) `react-hooks/refs` "Cannot access refs during render … Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render" on `onClick={() => run(item)}` → removed `restoreTo.current?.focus()` from `close()` and moved it into the open-effect's cleanup. - **Stale-payload calendar bug (found via live data, not tests):** the published blob has `last 2026-07-16` while today is `2026-08-15`. `withLiveToday` appended today directly after the last published day, breaking the consecutive-day invariant `buildActivityWeeks` relies on — every cell would have landed on the wrong weekday. Fixed by zero-filling the gap. - **Data-honesty bug in the same area:** because `sevenDayMinBaseline` filters `tokens > 0`, the projection produced `4,723,753 tokens so far today` from month-old July data. Fixed by gating the live cell on `fresh = shiftYmd(today, -1) <= lastPublished`; a stalled feed now renders zeros, no ring, no projection. - **My own bad test assertion:** asserted `dates.at(0)` to be `"2026-07-15"`, got `"2025-08-16"` — `materializeHistory` pads back 364 days before the window trim. Fixed to `expect(dates.at(0)).toBe(shiftYmd("2026-08-15", -(dates.length - 1)))`. - **Two failed `Edit` calls on `components/activity-section.tsx`** ("String to replace not found"). Root cause found via `sed -n '48,56p' components/activity-section.tsx | cat -et`: the fallback string on that line is a **non-breaking space** (`"M-BM- "` = U+00A0), not `" "`, so any `old_string` spanning that line fails to match. 5. **Problem Solving:** - Chose a column-per-week DOM for the heatmap specifically so mobile truncation is pure CSS (`nth-child` on columns) with zero JS and zero SSR/hydration divergence — replacing an earlier plan that would have needed a scroll-position effect or a month-matrix re-orientation. - Chose the listbox/option ARIA pattern over `role="grid"` because a column-major DOM cannot honestly present `role="row"`, and because 365 `

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent:** The user owns dhruv2mars.com (repo at `/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio`) and asked for a **complete from-scratch redo of the whole repo**, modeled on Chan Dai's site (https://dai.is-a.dev/, source at github.com/ncdai/chanhdai.com). A four-round grilling (pre-compaction) locked these decisions: - **Approach:** Rebuild in dai's *design idiom* with our *own information architecture* — NOT a fork, NOT a transcription. skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

# Design contract

Read before touching code. Supersedes the retired LEDGER contract (see `docs/adr/0005`).

## 0. Relationship to the Reference

dai.is-a.dev is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:

**Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.

**Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.

**Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.

The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.

## 1. Stack

Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · shadcn/ui on Radix + Base UI primitives ·
Motion for animation · `next-themes` · MDX via `next-mdx-remote` · Vercel. Latest stable at build
time. `bun` for everything.

## 2. Surfaces

```
/                 Masthead → AI Activity → Projects → footer      (single dense scroll)
/blog             hidden until the first real Post exists
/blog/[slug]      Post
/feed.xml         RSS                    ← survives from the old build
/writings         301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
/og               dynamic OG images
/sitemap.xml /robots.txt
404
```

`rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.

## 3. Masthead

One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name · `agentic engineer` · one line of positioning · social links
(x · github · linkedin · email).

**The avatar slot is a designed absence.** No portrait exists yet. Reserve the exact final footprint
and render a bordered placeholder that carries the same cursor-tracking light interaction a real
photo would. Empty shape, live behaviour. Dropping in a portrait later must be a one-line change with
zero layout shift. It must never read as a broken image.

## 4. AI Activity

The density anchor and the largest element above the fold. A year grid of day cells, intensity by
token count, with a hover/focus readout carrying the exact value — the readout is a fixed line, not a
floating tooltip, so nothing reflows. Lifetime total set large.

- Server-rendered with the real total present in the HTML before hydration. No skeleton, no
  client-only fetch, no hydration mismatch.
- One SVG, not hundreds of nodes. Grid semantics with a per-cell accessible name.
- Full keyboard traversal; the readout is an `aria-live` region.
- Below the tablet breakpoint the grid re-orients to a month matrix rather than scrolling
  horizontally. Every cell has a ≥24×24 hit area.
- Fixture fallback renders identically and is labelled `fixture`. Data is never invented.

## 5. Projects

Eight, curated, in this order. Tier 1 is the agentic thesis; Tier 2 earns its place on shipped craft.

```
01  relunar     CLI repro harness for coding agents          relunar.com
02  pi-queue    FIFO queue and steering for pi               published on npm
03  offdex      Local-first Codex across phone, web, native
04  gunmetal    Local OpenAI-compatible API over your existing subscriptions
05  mdv-ts      Terminal markdown editor, TypeScript + OpenTUI
06  block       WebGPU generative logo explorer              live demo
07  codexchat   Subscription-backed inference chat, Rust
08  openutm-v0  Cross-platform UTM alternative
```

Rows, not cards — name, one line, language, year, outbound link. Hover reveals the destination host.
No thumbnails, no detail pages, no tag chips.

`pi-queue` shows **"published on npm"** as a fact and never a download counter — the real number is
too small to help. Revisit if relunar gains traction.

## 6. Type, colour, motion

**Type.** Geist Sans for language, Geist Mono for data and chrome (numbers, dates, labels, nav,
metadata, code). Tabular numerals globally — no number column ever reflows. Six sizes, no seventh.
Uppercase reserved for section labels only.

**Colour.** Dark is default and primary; light is a real design, not an inversion. Near-black rather
than pure black, near-white rather than pure white. One accent, used sparingly and enumerated in
code. Both themes must pass WCAG AA for all text; heatmap ramp steps below AA are never the sole
carrier of meaning — the readout always states the value.

**Motion.** Short and purposeful: hover ~150ms, entrance ~350ms, theme ~250ms. `Motion` is used only
where CSS genuinely cannot do the job. Nothing animates perpetually. Nothing parallaxes, pins, or
jacks the scroll. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes movement but keeps colour-only interaction
feedback.

## 7. Prohibitions

No empty sections. No placeholder or invented data. No "coming soon". No fake metrics. No box
shadows. No gradients except the heatmap ramp. No thumbnails or project detail pages. No hamburger
menu. No perpetual animation. No page-level fade on route change. No dashboard grammar.

## 8. Acceptance tests

1. `curl` of `/` contains the real lifetime token total; console shows no hydration mismatch.
2. At 1440×900 the masthead and the complete year grid are visible without scrolling.
3. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 2560.
4. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390.
5. Full keyboard traversal of the heatmap, with the readout announced.
6. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
7. Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical (no perpetual motion).
8. No section renders with zero real items — including Blog, which stays hidden at zero Posts.
9. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, accessibility 100, best practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
10. `/writings` still 301s to `/blog`; `/feed.xml` still validates.
